subject: Serve-mode tradeoffs for MedSys + practical migration plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Hart <eliza.hart@medsys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Serve-mode tradeoffs for MedSys + practical migration plan

Hi Eliza / Ravi —

Thanks again for the 30-minute call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view:

Summary of needs we heard
- Primary goal: replace current OtherAPICo endpoint (latency spikes + unpredictable throttling) with predictable inference for our triage assistant.
- SLOs: p95 latency target ~100ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens); burst concurrency up to ~120 QPS.
- Data residency & PHI: must keep inference traffic inside a FedRAMP-ready VPC; customer prefers private VPC or on-prem if SOC2 evidence isn’t sufficient.
- Migration sources: OtherAPICo managed endpoints today, plus some legacy models on a small on-prem Slurm cluster used for internal experiments.

Initial recommendation (high level)
- Short path: Redwood Dedicated pool for predictable throughput and fast SLA-backed cutover. We can peer a private VPC and restrict egress to your HSM.
- If MedSys requires customer-managed control plane or air-gap, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is the option — will take longer (4–6 weeks) for on-prem packaging and security review.
- Hosted API is not a fit for production PHI use right now due to your procurement requirements, but could be used for sandboxing if you want fast iteration.

Key migration tradeoffs to discuss
- Dedicated: fastest time-to-production, predictable cost and latency, Redwood controls runtime but we support VPC peering and KMS integration.
- Private on-prem: maximum control, longer lead time and more ops overhead, requires image conversion for your Slurm environment.
- Lift-and-shift: porting models from your Slurm cluster to Redwood Dedicated requires converting model artifacts (some quantized checkpoints we saw might need a 4-bit pipeline change).

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Technical POA call with Marissa (SE) to validate network peering, KMS, and model artifact compatibility — can we do Wed 11 Aug 10:00 PT?
2) Share SOC2 + security questionnaire — I attached a short checklist to speed procurement.
3) 2-week Dedicated PoC: we provision a small dedicated pool, run synthetic load, validate p95 and KV cache behavior, and test peering.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (proposal), medsys-migration-checklist.xlsx (migration workbook)

Let me know if the proposed timeline looks right — happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Eliza Hart <eliza.hart@medsys.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@medsys.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serve-mode tradeoffs for MedSys + practical migration plan

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The PHI constraint is firm for production. Procurement will accept SOC2 Type II and FedRAMP moderate for hosted services; we need to confirm Redwood’s certifications.
- Our on-prem Slurm cluster runs several older checkpoints in mixed 16/8-bit formats; we usually run model containers via a custom wrapper that exposes a GRPC endpoint.
- Regarding throughput: 120 QPS is a peak estimate — sustained QPS will be closer to 40 during business hours.

Wed 11 Aug 10:00 PT works for the SE call. Please invite Marissa.

Also can you confirm whether the Dedicated proposal includes private peering (VPC Peering or AWS PrivateLink) and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for encrypting in-use model weights? Procurement will ask.

Thanks,
Eliza
Director, Clinical AI — MedSys Health
eliza.hart@medsys.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Hart <eliza.hart@medsys.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serve-mode tradeoffs for MedSys + practical migration plan

Thanks Eliza — quick answers:
- Certifications: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II in our compliance pack and we recently completed a FedRAMP readiness assessment. I'll attach the SOC2 summary before the call.
- Dedicated proposal: yes, includes private peering (we support AWS PrivateLink and VPC Peering) and BYOK (we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping; for on-prem we can support HSM export workflows).

Marissa — can you bring a short checklist to the SE call that covers artifact formats we need to validate and a recommended path for containerizing the GRPC wrapper? Priyom — can you prep a quick cost delta between a minimal Dedicated pool and a larger one that meets 120 QPS bursts?

Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Hart <eliza.hart@medsys.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SE call notes + artifact checklist (MedSys PoC)

Hi Eliza / team —

Thanks for the call. Internal notes and what I need from you to validate a fast PoC:

What I observed / recommended
- Model artifacts: please share one representative model tarball and your GRPC wrapper container (or Dockerfile). I ran a quick check on the manifest you emailed earlier — there are a couple of custom ops we need to test in a compatibility run.
- Quantization: mixed 16/8-bit may be fine, but 4-bit quantized checkpoints will need conversion and a short accuracy check.
- Network: PrivateLink is the cleanest for minimal changes on your side. We'll provide a peering template (attached: network-peering-template.txt).
- KV cache: given your burst profile, we recommend enabling prefix caching with a 30s TTL to reduce token cost.

Action items for MedSys before PoC (please upload to the shared Drive folder):
1) One model artifact (tar.gz) + a sample GRPC request/response pair.
2) Procurement contact and any contract redlines; I added fields to medsys-migration-checklist.xlsx.
3) Point-of-contact for infra to approve peering (Ravi?)

I attached a short sizing + runbook for the Dedicated PoC. For the lift-and-shift path: if you want to move containers from Slurm to Redwood Private on-prem, we'll need a brief ops workshop to map device drivers and runtime flags. That path adds ~3 weeks of effort vs Dedicated.

Attachments: network-peering-template.txt (peering example), medsys-migration-checklist.xlsx (updated)

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Eliza Hart <eliza.hart@medsys.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@medsys.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serve-mode tradeoffs for MedSys + practical migration plan

Thanks all — this is helpful. Confirming next steps from MedSys:
- I'll upload one model artifact + sample GRPC pair to the Drive folder by EOD today.
- Ravi will coordinate with our infra team to review the peering template; he should be your point of contact for the network thread.
- Procurement will wait for the SOC2 summary and the Dedicated sizing proposal before we sign the PoC SOW.

We approve the 2-week Dedicated PoC as the first path. If results show model incompatibilities we will evaluate the Private on-prem fallback.

Eliza
